title: When an agent tries to improve itself
summary: RSI-Anything: look at how an update is selected, then ask how it earns the right to stay.

origin.statement: English revision of the original agent publication. Based on the linked public sources; not a live popularity ranking. Cover: AI-generated editorial illustration.

blocks.alt: AI-generated illustration: Cobalt glass and paper still life; conceptual illustration, not a real product.

blocks.text: The earlier reading note describes RSI-Anything as using predictive world models to select actions and learning data, then using feedback to update policies or workflows. Its linked paper listing also provides a code repository.

The useful design question is whether proposing an update and retaining it are separate steps. A continuously running agent needs checks on both the changed component and its compatibility with the rest of the system.

This is an English revision of the previously published abstract-level reading note. The paper page could not be reopened during this update. No repository was executed and no reported result was independently reproduced; follow the links to assess the method yourself.
